bullets: Ravens' primary place-kicker heading into Week 1 — a low-variance role, but a full-time job on a good offense.
One of the most accurate kickers in the league since entering the NFL, including elite long-range range — locked in as Dallas' K1 with no competition.
Detroit's starting kicker on one of the league's most efficient offenses — plenty of scoring opportunities behind a strong O-line.
Veteran incumbent, Houston's clear starting kicker with no camp competition reported.
Jacksonville's starting kicker, known for elite leg strength on long attempts — no competition for the job.
Among the most accurate kickers in the NFL in recent seasons on a defense-first Steelers team that often plays close games — strong weekly floor.
Longtime Seahawks starter with no reported competition — steady, low-variance K1 role.
San Francisco's starting kicker behind a run-heavy, red-zone-efficient offense under Kyle Shanahan.

Broke out as the overall WR10 in PPR last year (78/1,006/7); locked in as the Z-receiver in new OC Mike LaFleur's scheme with projected 110-120 targets — camp reports have him looking sharper than Marvin Harrison Jr. so far.
Widely projected as the 2026 fantasy #1 overall pick — back-to-back 1,400+ rush-yard seasons plus 60+ catches gives him a McCaffrey-type dual-threat ceiling.
Was seen in a camp "hold-in" (out of pads/helmet) during a portion of a recent practice, though still engaged in drills — worth monitoring, not currently tagged as an injury.
Clear WR1 with essentially no target competition (~30% target share); should produce top-10 WR numbers, with shaky QB play (Michael Penix Jr.) the main swing factor rather than his role.
Finished 2025 as the No. 2 fantasy TE in PPR; projected top-5 again in 2026 as one of Penix's top two targets alongside London.
Consensus QB2 for 2026, but coming off a down 2025 (16.5 PPG, career-low 349 rush yds) due to hamstring/back injuries — real risk, though his efficiency on throws past the sticks remains elite.

3rd-round rookie who has “vaulted into the WR2 conversation” behind Zay Flowers as Rashod Bateman faces a possible suspension — contested-catch specialist, realistic range ~500-700 yards with spike weeks.
Locked in as the top overall fantasy QB — top-9 in passing yards 5 of the last 6 years, top-7 in passing TDs every year, with real rushing/scramble equity on top.
One of Buffalo's two centerpiece fantasy assets alongside Allen; expect high TD upside given how often Buffalo runs near the goal line.
No current injury — sat out Buffalo's preseason finale only as a scheduled rest day, on track to lead the Week 1 backfield vs. Houston.
Signed a 4-year, $48M extension (up to $30M guaranteed) in August 2025, locking him in through 2029.
Sleeper-caliber TE1 upside (80/1,000/10 pace) after a 7 TD, 14.6 YPC 2025 — durability is the real question, but camp reports have his snap share trending up even with Knox/Hawes healthy.
2025 AP Offensive Rookie of the Year (70/1,014/7); profiles as a safe WR2 (~WR18-20) capped by Carolina's low-volume passing offense, with Jalen Coker now adding real target competition.
Carolina's presumptive WR2 behind McMillan, averaging 10.1 PPG (half-PPR) over his last 9 games played in 2025 — health (missed 6 games) is the swing factor.
Chicago's clear RB1 in Ben Johnson's scheme — career highs in rush yards/TDs last season.
Sept 3 practice scare turned out to be cramping, not a leg injury — practiced Monday (Sept 7) and is on track to play Week 1 vs. Carolina.
Primed for a real Year 2 breakout under Ben Johnson — closed 2025 with 7 straight multi-passing-TD games and 9 games with a 10+ yard rush.
Heel contusion had him limited, but recent reports have him back to normal practice work — trending toward playing Week 1, though not 100% locked in yet.
Still a reliable WR2 with league-winning upside if Chase misses time — finished 2025 as the overall WR12 despite three Jake Browning starts dragging his average down.
Elite passing-volume QB1 if he stays healthy — the concern for fantasy drafters is ADP/price more than his ceiling.
Top-5, arguably top-3 PPR RB potential — posted 7 top-12 weekly finishes even through Burrow's 2025 absence; Samaje Perine remains mild committee/handcuff risk.

Rookie 1st-round pick competing with fellow rookie Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy for the top WR job — early camp buzz has him leapfrogging Jeudy, though Cleveland's offense projects as one of the league's weakest.
Franchise-tagged ($27.3M) after a 2025 breakout — 93 rec/1,429 yds/9 TD, top-6 PPR WR despite sharing targets with Lamb.
Coming off a down 2025 (75/1,077/3, worst yardage since his rookie year) but still a Round 2 pick — expected bounce-back with Pickens locked in alongside him.
QB7 in fantasy PPG in 2025 (4,552 yds/30 TD/10 INT); with both Lamb and Pickens back, worth drafting as a true QB1.
Named the clear Week 1 RB1 on Denver's own depth chart, ahead of RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman — has been a full participant in camp with no injury designation.
5.0 YPC on 15.3 att/game last year; profiles as a high-end starter given the touch security, though his injury history still adds real season-long variance.
QB15 range if healthy — Denver added Jaylen Waddle to a receiving corps already featuring Sutton/Franklin/Bryant/Mims/Engram, arguably his best supporting cast yet.
Likely slides to a true WR2 role now that Waddle is in town — real target competition caps his ceiling versus prior seasons.
Consensus #1 overall RB entering 2026 — 21+ PPR PPG in each of the last two seasons, with Montgomery's departure adding even more goal-line/touchdown equity.
Told reporters this week he expects to play and feels "near 100 percent," playing down the earlier back/hamstring concern — Isiah Pacheco's IR stint (MCL sprain) further cements the workhorse role.
Top-5 fantasy WR three years running (WR4 in PPG each of the last 3 seasons) — high floor, high ceiling, first-round caliber.
Coming off a big season but genuinely boom/bust (WR41 pace Weeks 1-10 vs. WR13 pace Weeks 11-18) — more of a WR3 with real week-winning upside than a lineup lock.
Favorite for the outside WR spot opposite Watson after a quiet rookie year, but real skepticism here — didn't produce even when Reed/Watson missed time as a rookie.
Slot role behind Watson/Golden — talented but inconsistent profile, a real but capped role.
Dealing with a foot/ankle sprain in camp; the team doesn't view it as long-term and he's "hopeful" to be back before Week 1 vs. Minnesota.

Became the presumptive Packers RB1 once Josh Jacobs was placed on the NFL's Commissioner Exempt List (Aug 30) amid a legal case that bars him from the team — Kaleb Johnson (acquired via trade from Pittsburgh) is the complementary back behind Lloyd.

Recovering from a second ACL tear; per GM Brian Gutekunst, expected to open the season on the PUP list, which would sideline him for at least the first four games with an earliest return around Week 5.
Would have profiled as the Packers' clear outside/X WR1 once healthy, but Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed take over the target volume in his absence.
Still a fantasy WR1 (ESPN ranks him WR10) — three straight 1,000-yard seasons, 21 TDs over that stretch.
Healthy and entrenched as Houston's clear WR1 target hog heading into Week 1.
Ranked QB11 for 2026 — with Etienne now gone to New Orleans, more of the offense funnels through Lawrence's arm and legs; expected to throw 30+ TDs for the first time.
Sent home from Sept 2 practice with an illness (not injury) — minor, expected fine well ahead of the Week 1 opener vs. CLE.
Ranked RB23 — real role in a backfield alongside Chris Rodriguez, but more of an “after the pass game is established” ground piece than a bell-cow.
Healthy and in true WR1 territory — averaged 18.8 PPR PPG and 9.8 targets/game across 8 games in 2025.
Coaching staff is confident he'll not just play Week 1 but "look like himself" post offseason knee-debris surgery.
A distant WR2 behind Rice — only a 16.1% target share and WR60 finish in 2025; deep-threat/boom upside but not a reliable weekly starter.
Posted 286.8 fantasy points in 2025 (10th among QBs); new OC Mike McDaniel plus a healthy starting O-line raises his ceiling, with real rushing upside on top of his passing floor.
Locked in as a starter opposite Ladd McConkey now that Mike Williams retired; still a boom-or-bust profile in a run-first McDaniel scheme.
Reigning NFL MVP — led the league in passing yards (4,707) and TD passes (46) in 2025; real regression risk since his 2025 leaned on unsustainable red-zone efficiency.
Consensus TE1 entering year 3 — top-3 fantasy TE in both of his first two seasons.

Underwent a meniscus trim procedure Sept 8 for the camp knee injury; Adam Schefter reports he's expected to miss "a game or two," ruling him out for the Sept 14 opener vs. Miami with Michael Mayer starting in his place.
Down year by his own standard in 2025 (WR30 overall) but still finished 6th league-wide in target share (28.5%) — new QB Kyler Murray has a track record of feeding elite WR1s.
Listed RB1 on New England's first unofficial 2026 depth chart ahead of TreVeyon Henderson — handles early-down/short-yardage work.

Rough Week 1 debut of the new-weapons era: 23/33 for 178 yds, 1 TD, but 3 INTs — all in the 4th quarter, including a game-sealing pick in the end zone — in a 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game loss to Seattle. Added 47 rush yds. Called the turnovers "unacceptable" postgame; also lost top target A.J. Brown to an ankle injury mid-game.
Coming off a QB2-overall 2025 (20.7 PPG); Patriots traded for A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs, giving him real weapons — widely projected top-5 fantasy QB before Week 1's opener.
Firmly entrenched as the Giants' starter after a strong rookie stretch (2,200 pass yds/15 TD, plus 480 rush yds/9 rush TD) — real breakout candidate under new HC John Harbaugh.
2025 1st-round pick (25th overall, Ole Miss) — Giants traded up for him, sending their 2025 2nd, 3rd, and a 2026 3rd to Houston.
Elite volume floor even coming off a down 2025 — earned a 30%+ target share early last season and has topped 23% every year of his career.
Clear backup, not a starter — Breece Hall re-signed and remains the workhorse; Allen competes with Isaiah Davis for change-of-pace touches.
Elevated to Eagles' clear WR1 now that A.J. Brown was traded to New England.
Still hasn't returned to practice as of Sept 8 (hamstring), but the team remains unconcerned and he's still expected to play Week 1.
Coming off a career year (60/591/11, TE7 overall) and remains the unquestioned TE1 with Brown's 121 vacated targets up for grabs.
Elite bell-cow workload locked in — $16.75M guaranteed for 2026 all but assures a featured role, with projections clustering around 300 total touches.
Rookie 1st-rounder now atop Seattle's backfield after presumed starter Zach Charbonnet tore his ACL — clearest path to lead-back touches on the roster.
While Zach Charbonnet opens the season on PUP (ACL recovery), Seattle is running a real 3-way rotation with George Holani and Emanuel Wilson rather than handing Price a clean bell-cow role.

Starting QB Sam Darnold exited the Sept 9 opener with a hip injury (fracture already ruled out, MRI pending) — if Drew Lock starts under center for a stretch, Seattle could lean more run-heavy, a mild tailwind for Price's workload.
Signed a massive 5-yr/$265M extension; finished as a QB1-range fantasy scorer in every full season as a starter, behind a receiving corps upgraded with Mike Evans and Christian Kirk.
Real WR2/target-lead opportunity now that Mike Evans is gone, retaining strong trust from Baker Mayfield — but coming off a career-worst efficiency season and a brutal two-year injury history.

Still working back from ankle rehab with some conflicting reports on his Week 1 availability vs. Cincinnati — worth checking Tampa Bay's final Friday injury report; Jalen McMillan's neck strain is a separate factor that could boost Egbuka's role regardless.
Entrenched starter chasing a 5th straight 1,000-yard season — hit 1,000 rushing yards in each of the past 4 years.
Returned to practice Wednesday after minor foot soreness — no real Week 1 concern, still ahead of Tyjae Spears on the depth chart.
Elite, high-ceiling QB1 when healthy — finished as a top-5 fantasy QB in 2024 before 2025 injuries wrecked his season; Washington aggressively upgraded his weapons to protect his 2026 ceiling.
Washington enters 2026 near the top of the league in vacated targets/air yards; his rough 2025 (38/582/3 in 10 games) looks like an outlier tied to a holdout and injuries rather than decline.
Reigning Super Bowl champs and the #1-ranked defense in 2026 projections — led the NFL in scoring defense and led the league with 7 defensive/ST TDs in 2025. Elite, high-floor DST1.

Worth monitoring: starting QB Sam Darnold left the Sept 9 opener with a hip injury (fracture ruled out, MRI pending Thursday) — a prolonged absence with backup Drew Lock at QB could mean tougher field position/offensive support for the defense if it drags into multiple games.

Back-to-back DST7 finishes with Vic Fangio adding Jonathan Greenard and Riq Woolen to an already deep room. Opens vs. WSH and TEN (favorable), but carries the toughest full-season DST schedule of any team in 2026.
2nd-best fantasy DST in 2025, then added Myles Garrett and revamped the secondary this offseason — projected top-3 unit for 2026 with a strong offense limiting bad field position.
Top-10 in sacks and takeaways in 2025; opens 2026 vs. Arizona and Las Vegas, called the best 2-game starting schedule of any DST — legitimate top-10 season-long upside.

Led the NFL in pressure rate (30.5%) in 2025 with the entire starting defense returning — one of the “safer” DST bets, though a top-3-toughest early schedule may lag results behind the underlying talent.

Real personnel hit — lost Rashan Gary to Dallas and All-Pro Micah Parsons is expected out until around Week 6, together costing over 55% of 2025 sack production. Currently projected just 24th for the season; Weeks 2-3 (vs. NYJ, then ATL) are flagged as good streaming spots even shorthanded.

Top-10 fantasy finish in 2025, but that leaned on a soft schedule; added Dre'Mont Jones, Kevin Byard, and a 2nd-round pick. Real talent additions, but a much tougher 2026 slate makes them a regression candidate off last year's ranking.

Top-5 fantasy unit two years running under HC DeMeco Ryans, ranked 2nd for 2026 behind only Seattle — led the NFL in fantasy points per game (56.4) last season. Opens with tougher matchups (BUF, then CIN).

DST5 in points per game in 2025 (7.8 PPG) even with T.J. Watt missing three games, powered by 27 forced turnovers and 48 sacks. Secondary got shredded at times — free agents Jamel Dean and Jaquan Brisker were brought in to fix that, but this remains one of the league's oldest defensive units.
High-ankle sprain from the Aug 14 preseason game vs LV — HC Mike LaFleur is publicly optimistic about Week 1 vs. LAC, but a source close to the team pegs it as a genuine 50/50 call.
New OC Mike LaFleur is moving him around the formation more; averaged 12.8 PPG over his last 5 healthy 2025 games (low-end WR1 pace).
No current 2026 injury or concussion concern found — fully past the foot/heel issues that limited him late last season.
Returned to practice Sept 3 after a two-week absence with a quad contusion; the team fully expects him ready for Week 1 vs. Indianapolis.
Turns 32; 2025 was still elite (1,595 yds / 16 TD) with no decline signs yet, but a new play-caller and remade O-line add real variance this year.
Enters Week 1 vs. Indianapolis as Baltimore's clear lead back, with only Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali behind him on the depth chart.
High right-ankle sprain from camp; officially week-to-week but “progressing nicely” and tracking to play Week 1 vs BAL.

Listed RB1 over Jonathon Brooks, but Carolina is running a real committee to open the year.
Hamstring issue has resolved — back to full practice, and HC Dave Canales confirmed Monday (Sept 7) he's expected ready for Week 1 vs. Chicago.
Listed RB1 over Jonathon Brooks, but Carolina is running a real 1A/1B committee to open the year.
Missed multiple practices this week (Tue/Wed) with unspecified soreness — not a new knee issue — but HC Dave Canales says he's "very optimistic" Brooks will be available for Week 1 vs. Jacksonville.
Opens the season in a real 1A/1B committee with Chuba Hubbard even once healthy.
Groin injury appears resolved — increased practice participation points to an on-track Week 1 status vs. Carolina.
Sidelined since mid-August with a hyperextended knee, labeled week-to-week by HC Ben Johnson — Week 1 availability remains genuinely uncertain.
DJ Moore's trade away clears the target volume for him as Caleb Williams' clear WR1 entering Ben Johnson's second year as HC.

Left Monday's (Sept 7) practice with a right leg injury and is listed day-to-day, but walked off under his own power and Ben Johnson has said he believes Odunze is trending toward being active for the opener at Carolina.
Moore's departure opens a big target vacuum; Bears leaning into more 13-personnel — projected ~78 rec/918 yds/7 TD after closing his rookie year red-hot.
2025 1st-round pick (10th overall, Michigan).
Hyperextended his knee in late August but has looked like full/normal work in recent practice reports — on track for Week 1 vs. Tampa Bay.
Moved to the unambiguous RB1 spot on Cleveland's depth chart, ahead of Sampson and Sanders.
Battling a minor "nagging" injury that cost him two camp practices, but coaches aren't concerned — remains Cleveland's clear lead back over Dylan Sampson, Raheim Sanders, and Ahmani Marshall.
2025 2nd-round pick (36th overall, Ohio State), acquired via a Day 1 trade with Jacksonville.
Led the Browns in receiving as a rookie (72/731/6); with Njoku gone he's the unquestioned TE1 under new OC Todd Monken, who developed Andrews and Likely.
Hip injury flare-up from a recent practice hit — returned to full practice (individual + team drills) Tuesday, trending positive for the Sept 13 opener vs. New Orleans.
Confirmed "full-go" for Week 1 vs. Minnesota after full-contact clearance and full participation in a joint practice vs. Arizona — a clean upgrade off the torn ACL, though still his first year back.

Pleaded no contest Sept 10 to misdemeanor battery and criminal-damage charges from the May incident — fined $1,000 plus costs, with the damage charge to be dismissed after a 12-month deferred agreement.

The legal resolution does NOT end his NFL absence: the league says there is "no change to his status" and he remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List while a separate personal-conduct-policy review continues, with a suspension (some Packers reporters estimate 4-6 games) still expected; unclear if the league rules before Sunday's opener at Minnesota, so treat him as unplayable/bench for now.
Green Bay has already hedged, trading a 2028 6th-round pick to Pittsburgh for RB Kaleb Johnson as depth-chart insurance — a real sign the team isn't banking on a quick Jacobs return.
Minor calf injury — full return to practice Tuesday, on track to be a full participant or off the injury report entirely for the Ravens opener.
Limited in practice this week with a heel/ankle issue, but HC Shane Steichen said Sept 9 "he should be good" to play the Sept 13 opener vs. Baltimore — could still open on a snap count.
His role grew even more important after Indianapolis traded Michael Pittman Jr. to Pittsburgh in March, clearing out the WR2 competition.
Groin injury has fully resolved in practice — by all accounts a full go for Week 1 vs. Baltimore.
Traded from LV to Jacksonville to bolster a banged-up WR room.
Told reporters Wednesday (Sept 9) he will play Week 1 vs. Cleveland despite practicing in a non-contact pinnie for the lingering hand injury.
Back to full practice as of Tuesday — the shoulder concern is no longer in doubt for the Week 1 opener vs. Cleveland, Jacksonville's clear WR1.
Stepped up in practice reps amid Thomas/Meyers injuries in one of the league's deepest WR rooms, alongside Travis Hunter.
Free-agent signing (3yr/$43.05M, not a trade) after being Super Bowl LX MVP with Seattle.
Had some ankle/foot swelling in late August, but is expected ready for the Week 1 opener.
Andy Reid confirmed him as the Week 1 starter vs. Denver, having practiced fully with no missed sessions since clearing his ACL/LCL recovery in July.
Now 37, the oldest TE in the league; production down two straight years (11.4 PPG in 2025, worst since 2015) — projected for a further step down (74/770/4).
Denver's own Week 1 depth chart lists him as RB2 behind J.K. Dobbins, not the lead role previously expected — likely limited to third-down/passing-game work early on.
Drafted 60th overall in the 2025 draft — entering his 2nd NFL season in 2026, not a rookie.
Acquired via trade from MIA in March 2026; forms the new top of Denver's WR room with Courtland Sutton, who may shift toward a red-zone/3rd-down role.
On track for Week 1 after a full practice return — the earlier camp strain has fully resolved.
Real committee with David Montgomery — locked into 3rd-down/receiving work and kick returns rather than a clean backup role.

Trade acquisition from DET leads the Houston backfield, and Joe Mixon's release clears out the only other real competition — but Woody Marks still holds real passing-down/receiving touches, so it remains a genuine committee, not a clear lead back.
Carries no injury designation heading into Week 1 vs. Arizona — the ambiguity from his Aug 27 preseason-finale kickoff hit has cleared, and he's back handling the full kicking/kickoff workload.
Now the clear WR1 with Keenan Allen gone, leading the room over Quentin Johnston.
New OC Mike McDaniel (replacing Greg Roman) should reopen the passing scheme in his favor.
Rookie hype exceeds his current role — projected ~250 att/1,125 yds, but likely won't clear 70% snap share with Mitchell handling passing downs. High-variance breakout, not a lock.

Played through the groin/legal-matter uncertainty with no issue — started and finished the Sept 10 opener in Melbourne, a 27-7 loss to San Francisco. Posted 5 catches for 74 yards (no TD); was stopped just short of the goal line on a key red-zone snap, and a deep shot intended for him was picked off by Renardo Green.
Still the clear focal point of the Rams passing game even in a tough offensive day for the whole unit (Stafford: 15/25, 155 yds).
Turns 33; 2025 TD rate was unsustainable (49% of his fantasy points came via red-zone scores vs. a 14.5% NFL average) and his catch rate hit a career-low 53%.
No longer the clear #1 target with Nacua sharing the offense — real regression risk.
Remains the lead back in a McVay-preferred ~65:35 split with Blake Corum — not under real threat, but not a bell-cow either.
RB2 behind Kyren Williams in a ~65:35 split that has been fluid through camp.
Elevated to Rams' primary kicker after a strong rookie year: 18/19 FG, 48/48 PAT.
Joshua Karty demoted to backup (not cut) — Mevis holds the job outright for now.

Off the injury report entirely (no designation) ahead of the Sept 13 opener vs. Miami after a full practice week — the Aug 23 ankle sprain is no longer a Week 1 concern; rookie Mike Washington Jr. remains the primary backfield backup.
No current injury flag, but missed time each of the last two seasons plus offseason shoulder surgery.
New OC Jeff Hafley is planning a massive workload (40-touch game talk) — huge weekly ceiling, real durability risk.
Officially co-starter with Aaron Jones, but took the lead role in 2025 (159 carries to Jones' 132) and camp reports again favor him for the larger early-season share.
Co-starter on paper with Jordan Mason, who has outproduced and outworked him in camp — likely the smaller half of the split early on.
Rough 2025: a 3-game suspension to start the year, only 17.4% target share (Jefferson had 28.2%), finished WR43.
QB upgrade to Kyler Murray helps, but MIN also signed WR Jauan Jennings — adds competition rather than clearing it. Profiles more WR3/bench right now.

Officially ruled OUT by the Patriots (announced Sept 8) for the Week 1 opener vs. Seattle after missing all three practices this week with the ankle injury — Rhamondre Stevenson is the confirmed must-play lead back.

Left his Patriots debut early in the 3rd quarter of the Sept 9 NFL Kickoff Game (a 13-10 loss to Seattle) with a right ankle injury after Seahawks CB Nehemiah Pritchett's knee landed on his ankle; had 3 catches for 26 yds on 4 targets before exiting.

Spotted in a walking boot postgame and got X-rays; HC Mike Vrabel had no update afterward ("Wasn't able to return, obviously"). No official diagnosis yet, but outside medical opinions have flagged a possible high-ankle sprain (or worse), which would typically cost multiple weeks — real risk to his Week 2+ availability.

Arrived via trade from PHI (Patriots sent Philadelphia a 2028 1st-round pick and a 2027 5th-round pick); signed for up to $112.75M with $32.75M guaranteed. Was stepping into a wide-open target share atop New England's WR room before the injury.
Signed in free agency; profiles as a high-volume slot piece similar to Diggs' old role now that Diggs is gone.
Hamstring injury in an August joint practice vs JAX; placed on IR with a return designation — out at least the first 4 games.
History of 4+ documented concussions from 2022-2024, but played all of 2025 concussion-free and projects as the clear WR1 again (WR8 in points/game last year).
Signed a 4-yr/$52M deal with hometown New Orleans as a free agent and is listed as the starter.
Alvin Kamara remains on the roster (health TBD) alongside Kendre Miller — real early-season committee risk.
Recovering from a November 2025 ACL/meniscus tear; releasing WR Darius Slayton read as an early bullish signal on his Week 1 outlook.
Practiced fully Wednesday (Sept 9) and is trending toward playing the SNF opener vs. Dallas after clearing post-practice medical checks.

Fully cleared from last year's gruesome rookie ankle injury (dislocation + open fracture) and confirmed as the Giants' Week 1 starting RB over Tyrone Tracy Jr., hosting Dallas on Sunday Night Football.
Signed for 3yr/$40M+, now the clear TE1 ahead of Theo Johnson, reunited with HC John Harbaugh — real path to a top-10 fantasy TE role after sharing looks with Mark Andrews in Baltimore.
Nostalgic reunion signing; realistically a WR160-caliber depth/leadership piece with no real fantasy relevance in 2026.
Groin issue trending better — HC Aaron Glenn confirmed he'd practice this week and is expected ready for the Sept 13 opener vs. Tennessee.
20th overall pick, stepping into the WR2 role behind DeVonta Smith with A.J. Brown gone.
Hamstring strain in camp plus Philly's low-volume passing scheme caps his rookie-year ceiling — realistic WR4 as a rookie.
His camp hamstring strain is also trending back toward full practice participation as of Sept 3.

Trade finalized March 9, 2026: Colts sent him plus a 2026 7th-round pick to Pittsburgh for a 2026 6th-round pick — as part of the trade-and-sign, the Steelers also signed him to a new 3-year, $59M contract.

Practiced Monday (Sept 7) with his new team for the first time this camp; calls himself "hopeful" for the Sept 13 opener vs. Atlanta, but hamstring recovery means his role/snap share could still be limited even if he plays.
Undisclosed injury, also expected to play Week 1 vs ATL.
Traded from Seattle to Pittsburgh in 2025 (Steelers sent a 2nd- and 7th-rounder, got back a 6th) and signed a 5-year, $150M extension there.
Steelers' first depth chart lists Jaylen Warren as RB1 and Dowdle as RB2, despite reports Dowdle earned first-team camp reps.
HC Mike McCarthy — his coach in Dallas — wants a real 1A/1B committee, not a clear lead back.
Signed with Pittsburgh in free agency on a 2-year, $12.25M deal, arriving from Carolina (originally Dallas).

Confirmed as Pittsburgh's Week 1 RB1 on the team's own depth chart over Rico Dowdle, and beat reporting now describes him as the clear starter — though Dowdle is still expected to see meaningful early-down work in a timeshare.
Signed a 2-year extension through 2027 (~$17.5M total, $12M guaranteed) in September 2025.

Opened 2026 with 8 catches for 122 yds and the game-winning 45-yard TD (41 YAC) on 4th-and-1 in the 4th quarter of Seattle's 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game win over New England — early sign the regression fears may be overblown.

Backup QB Drew Lock (18/22, 187 yds) finished that game after starter Sam Darnold left with a hip injury on the opening drive; Darnold's Week 2 status is worth tracking since it affects who's throwing him the ball.
Led all NFL WRs with 1,793 yds/10 TD in 2025 and won Offensive Player of the Year; now the highest-paid WR in history (4yr/$168.6M).
Top-5 overall fantasy asset — the question is regression off a historic year, not upside.

Good news for his QB situation: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said postgame that doctors have ruled out a hip fracture for Darnold — an MRI Thursday (Sept 10) will determine the actual return timetable.
Full workhorse usage in the opener with no ill effects from the calf scare: 10 carries for 68 yards plus 5 catches for 20 yards in the win over the Rams.
Held out of the end zone, but the touch volume is exactly what you want to see after last year's injury history.
Debut with his new team went well: 6 catches for 49 yards and a TD in the 27-7 win over the Rams in Melbourne — the Purdy upgrade already showing up on the stat sheet.
Turns 33 in August; worth watching for the usual wear-down-the-stretch pattern, but no concerns after Week 1.

Played in the opener as expected off the Achilles recovery, but usage was light (2 catches, 12 yards on 5 targets) — matches Shanahan's stated plan to manage his snap count, worth watching if that workload increases in Week 2.

Left the Sept 10 season opener vs. the Rams in Melbourne in the 2nd quarter with a non-contact left ankle injury and did not return (no catches); HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed his Achilles is intact but couldn't say whether it's a high-ankle sprain, with an MRI pending back in the Bay Area to determine severity.

Rookie with real preseason buzz (11 catches in two preseason games) as a deep-league breakout stash if SF's crowded WR room opens up targets — but hold off starting him anywhere until the MRI results clarify how many games he'll miss.
Two straight down seasons (sub-12 PPG each) with the worst YPRR marks of his career and a shrinking red-zone role.
Back in SF on a 1-year “reunion” deal — real chance 2026 is his last fantasy-relevant year.
Toe sprain has limited him since camp opened — missed Tuesday's practice too, adding some uncertainty, but HC Todd Bowles is still "hopeful" for the Sept 13 opener vs. Cincinnati.
Now locked in as Tampa Bay's WR1 with Mike Evans gone to SF.
Buccaneers' own depth chart lists him as RB1 over Bucky Irving — a real battle, expect close to a 50/50 split. His receiving-back role (73 catches last year) could cap Irving's ceiling.
